The '''1926 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 40th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship began on 18 April 1926 and ended on 24 October 1926.

The championship was won by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] who secured the title following a 4–6 to 2–0 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Roll of Honour |publisher=The GAA website |access-date=27 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110905085701/http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |archive-date=5 September 2011 }}</ref> This was their 8th All-Ireland title.

[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] were the [[1925 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]] but were defeated by Cork in the Munster final.

[[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] won the [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship|Ulster SHC]] title, but at the suggestion of the Central Council, it was decided that the Ulster winners would enter the All Ireland Junior Hurling Championship.<ref>Irish Independent 1905–current, Friday, 10 December 1926; Page: 12</ref>

==Championship statistics==
===Miscellaneous===

* The Munster final between [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] is abandoned after just ten minutes when the crowd storm the field.{{fact|date=August 2022}}
* For the first time ever the Munster final goes to a second replay.{{fact|date=August 2022}}
* The All-Ireland semi-final between [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Galway GAA|Galway]] is the first GAA game to be broadcast on radio. The commentator is [[P.D. Mehigan]].  It is also the first commentary on a field game to take place in [[Europe]].{{fact|date=August 2022}}
